title: SKP Orchestrator
description: Orchestrator control plane -- 3 replicas across 5 queues. Six pipeline panels are shared with the processor board and generated from one source so the two cannot drift.

list.name: role
list.label: Role
list.description: Applies only to the produced / consumed / produce-duration panels -- the three instruments that carry a role attribute. See the note panel on the pipeline tier.

panels.title: Consuming
panels.description:
0 means no consumer tag on at least one queue -- nothing is listening. No other signal answers this.

Restricted to replicas that have reported in the last 40s: a dead replica's gauge is held at its last value by the collector and by Prometheus's lookback, so an unrestricted min() reads the posture of processes that no longer exist.

panels.title: L2 gate
panels.description: The single best answer to 'why did the pipeline stop'. 0 means the gate is shut and deliveries are being requeued.

panels.title: Hydration admitted
panels.description: One-shot readiness. Separates 'not consuming because the store is down' from 'not consuming because the first hydration pass has not finished'.

panels.title: Leaders elected
panels.description:
Must be exactly 1. Followers reading 0 is by design and is NOT a fault -- StepOutcomeHandler is deliberately not leader-gated, so a follower is still expected to consume. Zero means nobody holds the lease; two means a split.

This one stat did fall when all three replicas were deleted, and it is worth knowing why it was able to: a leader releases its lease on graceful shutdown and the SDK flushes that final export, so the gauge genuinely reached 0. A replica killed outright leaves it held at 1. Do not read a departure off this panel -- read it off Workers missing on SKP Flow.

panels.title: Not acked
panels.description:
Deliveries the consumer refused or sent back, COUNTED over the visible range. Drill into 'reason' on the pipeline tier for why.

Counted rather than rated. Measured at the old 60s export cadence, when the rate window here was 240s: as a rate this read 0.00 through every scenario in the chaos suite, because the single parked delivery the broker outage produced was 1/240 = 0.004, which rounds to nothing at any sane precision. The window is 60s now, which makes that same delivery 0.017 -- still nothing at this precision, which is why the panel is still counted rather than rated.

targets.expr: ((sum(increase(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",disposition=~"requeued|parked"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) > (sum(max_over_time(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",disposition=~"requeued|parked"}[$__range])) or vector(0))) or (sum(max_over_time(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",disposition=~"requeued|parked"}[$__range])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Ack lost
panels.description: The silent case: the handler ran to completion but the broker never heard the ack, so it will redeliver. Cause is on the channel-resets panel. Counted over the range, for the reason 'Not acked' gives.

targets.expr: ((sum(increase(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",disposition="acked",landed="false"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) > (sum(max_over_time(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",disposition="acked",landed="false"}[$__range])) or vector(0))) or (sum(max_over_time(pipeline_messages_consumed_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",disposition="acked",landed="false"}[$__range])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Egress faults
panels.description:
unroutable = the queue is not declared. transient = the broker is unreachable. Opposite remedies; this is the only signal that separates them.

Counted over the range. Scaling the broker to zero for sixty seconds produced exactly two transient publishes; as a rate they were 0.00 on every board and the only trace of them anywhere was a new legend entry on the produced-by-outcome timeseries.

targets.expr: ((sum(increase(pipeline_messages_produced_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",outcome=~"transient|unroutable|refused"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) > (sum(max_over_time(pipeline_messages_produced_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",outcome=~"transient|unroutable|refused"}[$__range])) or vector(0))) or (sum(max_over_time(pipeline_messages_produced_total{service_name=~"$service_name",service_version=~"$service_version",service_instance_id=~"$service_instance_id",outcome=~"transient|unroutable|refused"}[$__range])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Channel resets
panels.description: Channel churn over the visible range. The cause of ack loss.

panels.title: Produced by type and outcome
panels.description: Egress. outcome != accepted is a fault.

panels.title: Consumed by type and disposition
panels.description: Ingress. Exactly one increment per delivery, on every exit path of the consumer.

panels.title: Produce duration p95 / p99
panels.description:
A real broker round-trip to publisher confirmation, not the time to write a frame.

The mean rides alongside the quantiles deliberately. It comes from sum/count and so is independent of bucket boundaries -- if it ever diverges wildly from p50, the ladder has stopped fitting the data. That is exactly how the millisecond-ladder defect was caught: p95 read 4.9s while the mean read 15ms.

panels.title: Consumer inflight by queue
panels.description: Deliveries inside a handler. PrefetchCount is 1, so a sustained 1 is saturation -- the threshold line marks it.

panels.title: Channel resets by reason
panels.description: shutdown, recovered, reopened. Each renumbers delivery tags and is what makes landed=false possible.

panels.title: Consuming by queue
panels.description:
Per-queue view of the verdict stat. A queue reading 0 while the others read 1 is one wedged consumer, not an outage.

Aggregated by queue on this board because each queue has one consumer. The processor board splits this per replica, where every replica shares one queue.

A line that ENDS is a replica that left; a line at 0 is one that is present and not consuming.

Unfilled on purpose: the orchestrator has five queues, all sitting at 1 in health, and five filled areas stacked on one line render as a single opaque block in which a dip is invisible.

panels.title: Leader by replica
panels.description: Explains why cron fires land on one replica. Only cron fires are fenced by leadership.

panels.title: Dispatch by destination
panels.description: Per-processor fan-out from this side of the hop.

panels.title: Consumed by role
panels.description: The role attribute records what this replica was AT THE TIME it handled the delivery, so a replica carries both values across a leadership change. It is not a replica selector -- service_instance_id is.

options.content:
`role` is an attribute on **three instruments only**: `pipeline.messages.produced`, `pipeline.messages.consumed` and `pipeline.produce.duration`. Verified against the live stack.

The gauges (`gate.open`, `leader`, `hydration.admitted`, `consumer.consuming`, `consumer.inflight`) and `consumer.channel.resets` carry **no** `role`, so the filter is applied only to the four panels that can honour it. Applying it board-wide would empty the rest, because a `role=~"leader"` matcher does not match a series that has no `role` label.

The verdict tier is deliberately left unfiltered as well: it answers *is anything wrong anywhere*, and a role selection there would let a follower fault hide behind a leader view.

panels.title: Thread-pool queue length
panels.description: Explains consumption stalling while the gate is open and the consumer still reports consuming=1: callbacks are starved, not blocked.

panels.title: GC pause time
panels.description: Seconds of GC pause per second. Explains duration p99 spikes with no broker or dependency fault.

panels.title: Exception rate
panels.description: Correlates with rising parked / refused dispositions and with faulted process outcomes.

panels.title: Process restarts
panels.description: A monotonic counter going backwards means the process is new. The one signal that explains a simultaneous gap in every other series.
